anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level SQL or transaction design forces the engine to process more data, rows, or time than business logic truly requires.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk pages or index structures are physically or logically corrupt, making access paths and stored data unreliable.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Physical or logical free space in data, log, temp, or backup areas is exhausted, hitting hard allocation limits.

When all three anomalies manifest together, the system exhibits a blended symptom set: queries that already scan or modify excessive data stumble into corrupted pages, returning inconsistent row counts, checksum errors, or forced full-table scans. The extra I/O, temp sorting, and bloated undo/redo generated by the inefficient workload rapidly consume remaining space, leading to allocation failures for data pages, temp segments, or archive logs. Space exhaustion, in turn, halts index rebuilds, corruption repairs, and normal checkpoint or log-recycle operations, so corruption symptoms and slow-query entries grow unmitigated. Users observe a mix of long-tail latencies, intermittent "row not found" or duplication errors, unexpected full-scan plans, and sudden "no space left" or "cannot extend" failures, often within the same session.

Causal chain: Poorly written SQL drives large scans and massive DML, inflating data and log footprints and steadily eroding available space. Shrinking free space increases the likelihood of partial writes, failed auto-extends, and out-of-space conditions during critical write-ahead logging or page splits, which can introduce new corruption or leave indexes half-updated. Existing corruption forces the optimizer to abandon damaged indexes and fall back to even broader scans, multiplying the workload’s space and I/O consumption. Repair attempts, re-writes, or repeated application retries further bloat logs and temp usage. Thus, each anomaly intensifies the others: logical inefficiency accelerates space depletion; space pressure elevates corruption risk and blocks remediation; corruption feeds back by degrading access paths, amplifying the workload footprint and pushing the system toward a cascading failure state.

entry.official_definition: Specifies how long transmitted data may remain unacknowledged before the TCP connection is forcibly closed.
entry.trigger_condition: TCP data sent by PostgreSQL remains unacknowledged longer than tcp_user_timeout on systems supporting TCP_USER_TIMEOUT.
entry.workload_impact: The TCP connection is forcibly closed.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
